summary: Describes how Static Context Header Compression and fragmentation work with 3GPP Narrowband IoT. It has a normative part specifying use over NB-IoT and an informational part recommending values for 3GPP.

plainLanguage.summary: Tiny devices on cellular networks have little room, so this shows how to shrink message headers on that kind of link.

questions: how to fragment packets on nb-iot
how does schc work over nb-iot
subtitle: How to squeeze IPv6 headers and fragment packets for tiny devices on cellular Narrowband IoT links.

tldr.problem: Narrowband IoT devices send very small amounts of data over a cellular network, and full IP headers waste much of the little room that each radio transmission has.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC places SCHC header compression and fragmentation in the application layer, on top of the network's Non-IP Data Delivery service, and recommends parameter values. It also suggests, informationally, how 3GPP itself could use SCHC inside the radio link and the control plane.
tldr.outcome: The normative part gives an application a way to use SCHC over NB-IoT without changing the 3GPP architecture; the informational part is only a set of suggestions to 3GPP.

today: RFC 9391 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2023. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why SCHC Meets NB-IoT
sections.content:
RFC 9391 describes how Static Context Header Compression and fragmentation (SCHC), defined in RFC 8724 and RFC 8824, can be used with the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) and Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT). NB-IoT is described as a 3GPP Low-Power WAN technology based on the LTE architecture, with extra optimization for IoT and a narrowband spectrum frequency. The document assumes NB-IoT functionality of 3GPP release 15.

The document has two parts. The normative part says how any application must use SCHC over the 3GPP public service. The informational part describes how 3GPP could use SCHC in its own protocol stack.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a walkie-talkie where each message can only be a few words long. This document shows how to shorten the address on each message so more of the message is real content.

sections.title: The NB-IoT Network Architecture
sections.content:
NB-IoT relies on several Network Gateways (NGWs), possibly from different providers. Data can take different paths, each with its own bandwidth, acknowledgments and link-layer reliability and segmentation. A device (Dev-UE) talks to a radio gateway (RGW-eNB), which reaches the core. A path through the NGW-MME, the NGW-CSGW and the NGW-PGW may give a limited bandwidth, from a few bytes per second to one thousand bytes per second.

Another node, the NGW-SCEF, securely exposes service and network capabilities to entities outside the operator. Its main functions are path connectivity and device monitoring, and its data path is small.

The recommended 3GPP MTU size is 1358 bytes. The radio protocols limit packets over the air, including overhead, to 1600 bytes, but the recommended MTU is smaller to avoid fragmentation in the backbone, because payload encryption works in multiples of 16 and the core adds transport overhead.
sections.plainLanguage: A message from a small gadget passes through several relay stations on its way to the company that wants it, and some roads between stations are very narrow.

sections.title: Three Places to Put SCHC
sections.content:
Because 3GPP standardizes NB-IoT, adding SCHC inside the network would have to be specified in the NB-IoT standard. The RFC identifies three use cases.

  • Radio link: SCHC between the Dev-UE and the RGW-eNB (informational).
  • Control path: SCHC for packets sent over the NGW-MME or NGW-SCEF, called Data over Non-Access Stratum (DoNAS) (informational).
  • Non-IP Data Delivery (NIDD): SCHC in the application layer of the device and the Application Server, or a broker at the operator's edge (normative).

The first two are valid for any 3GPP architecture, not only NB-IoT, and involve the operator's internal network, so they are in the informational part. The normative scenarios do not modify the 3GPP architecture or any of its components; they use it only as a layer 2 transmission.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three spots where the shortening trick could happen: on the radio hop, on the control channel, or in the apps at both ends. Only the last one is something every app is told to do.

sections.title: SCHC over Non-IP Data Delivery
sections.content:
With NIDD, the application layer compresses packets with SCHC before sending them. Packets travel between the NGW-PGW (or NGW-SCEF) and the Application Server by IP tunnel or API call. Since compression happens before transmission, the network cannot understand the packet and holds no compression context, so it treats the packet as Non-IP traffic and delivers it directly over layer 2.

The application layer handles the static context, so context distribution MUST follow the application's capabilities. Scenarios MAY use SCHC header compression for IPv6 packets.

  • RuleID: SCHC overhead SHOULD NOT exceed the effective bits of the smallest physical Transport Block. Packets are byte-aligned, so the maximum SCHC header size is 12 bits for the smallest block. The RuleID may range from 2 bits (4 rules) to 8 bits (256 rules). With a 2-bit RuleID only 6 bits remain for the compression residue.
  • Packet size: the maximum RECOMMENDED MTU is 1358 bytes, because packets cross the whole 3GPP infrastructure, not just the radio.
  • Fragmentation: packets over 1358 bytes need SCHC fragmentation. The No-ACK mode MAY be enough in point-to-point connections, but ACK-on-Error is RECOMMENDED where packets may be lost before reaching the radio network.
sections.plainLanguage: The two apps agree on a secret shorthand before sending. The phone network just carries the squeezed notes without understanding them, and big notes get cut into pieces that are checked on arrival.

sections.title: Recommended Fragmentation Parameters
sections.content:
NB-IoT aligns data to bytes, so SCHC tries to reduce padding. The header size needs to be a multiple of 4, and tiles MAY keep a fixed size of 4 or 8 bits (2 bits when the transfer block is 16 bits). Two configurations are RECOMMENDED:

  • Transfer Blocks of 304 bits or fewer: an 8-bit header, with RuleID of 1 to 3 bits, DTag of 1 bit, FCN of 3 bits and W of 1 bit.
  • Transfer Blocks bigger than 304 bits: a 16-bit header, with RuleID of 8 to 10 bits, DTag of 1 or 2 bits, FCN of 3 bits and W of 2 or 3 bits.

A WINDOW_SIZE of (2^N)-1 is RECOMMENDED. The Reassembly Check Sequence follows the default size in RFC 8724, with a length equal to the L2 Word. MAX_ACK_REQ is RECOMMENDED to be 2, though applications MAY change it. Section 6 adds that the L2 Word for NB-IoT MUST be considered 8 bits, since 3GPP wireless access assumes a byte-aligned payload.

The RFC also notes that the Power Save Mode and Idle Mode DRX govern how often a device wakes, and that these modes allow the battery to last ten years. The Inactivity Timer and Retransmission Timer can be set based on the timer limits it describes.
sections.plainLanguage: The rules say how many bits each label part may use. A small block gets a tiny label and a big block gets a slightly larger one, so no space is wasted on filler.

sections.title: Informational Suggestions to 3GPP
sections.content:
This part consists of IETF suggestions to 3GPP. Over the radio link, SCHC would sit in the PDCP layer. The 3GPP architecture already supports Robust Header Compression (ROHC, RFC 5795) there, so SCHC entities could be deployed similarly without significant changes. The RLC layer already fragments in its Acknowledged and Unacknowledged modes, so SCHC fragmentation is unnecessary there and SHOULD NOT be used.

Over the Non-Access Stratum, DoNAS lets the device piggyback small uplink data into the initial uplink message and use pre-established security. The NAS layer already uses ROHC, so it can adopt SCHC too. The NGW-MME is the terminating node for NAS on the network side.

For both cases the RFC suggests the Radio Resource Control protocol configure SCHC and distribute the static context, as is done for ROHC. It assumes 9 bytes of radio protocol overhead (5 for PDCP, 4 for RLC and MAC), and a maximum packet size of 1600 bytes. SCHC fragmentation functions are disabled because RLC can segment packets to fit the selected block. The ACK-Always mode might help in the future when RLC runs in Transparent Mode.
sections.plainLanguage: If the phone company ever wants to use the shorthand itself, it could plug it in where it already does a similar trick. This part is advice, not a rule.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The Security Considerations section says the document does not add any security considerations and follows RFC 8724 and the 3GPP access security document specified in TS 33.122. The IANA Considerations section states that the document has no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: This document adds no new locks or keys. It relies on the ones the earlier rules and the phone network already have.
